title: New York with Fitzgerald, stranded, then Bert Kelly's call
summary: The band goes to New York for a Jolson show and the Low circuit; members drift home, Lopez shovels snow, and Bert Kelly sends for him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then we went, then, uh... Everybody wanted us. So finally, Frank Clark of Watterson, Butler & Snyder. The music publishers. He came down with a big hot idea that he had an agent coming in town. Harry Fitzgerald. Big agent. You know, we see Fitz. So Fitz comes down. Oh, he's got it all made for a New York show. Yeah, a New York show. We go to New York to, uh... to John and Jolson's show. A show called Dancing Around. Well, if you know Jolson, you know, he always had fights with these directors, producers, and everything. So we're in New York. Fitz brings us to New York, and then Jolson takes a party. He's gone to Florida. You know, he doesn't want nothing to do at the show. And then, there we are. So we fooled around with Fitz for a long time. Played a big party for Diamond and Jim Brady and the Dollar Sisters. And we played for, oh, up at Healy's, Bustonabies. And then finally, we went into the Low Time. Played about 20, 25 weeks for them. In the meantime, the boys all kind of got... One got a yen for home, see? Cold, snow, that's that and the other. So one by one, they took off. And left Tom Brown and I in New York. And we didn't go to the Union and didn't know anybody. So that was it. So then finally, Tom said, well, Ray, I can't make it. I said, it's really rough. In the meantime, little Gusty Miller, he left the band in Chicago, and he went over there with Bert Kelly. And Larry Shields joined us. And then Shields came up. We knew we'd known Shields down home, so you see. Sure. So all right. Then Shields, he went home. This old man was sick or something. And they caught that boat down at that Morgan Lander. For 19 bucks, they could go home and steer it, see? So he took off. So when Miller's in Chicago, I wired Miller. Asked him if there's anything doing around Chicago. So sure enough, he got in contact with Boy Kelly, and Kelly sent for me.
Did Tom Brown go with you, too?
No, Tom had gone down home.

He left, yeah. He left me by myself. Well, yeah, I don't blame him. He was, things were rough. Of course, I had my wife and kid, my oldest boy. And it was getting rough for me. I was shoveling snow in New York. And the sign says, Men wanted to shovel snow. 50 cents an hour on day, 75 cents an hour. I said, give me that night shift. I held that for about four or five nights.
Come on in, yeah. Come on in. I was talking about when you were shoveling snow even. Yeah.
My brother was making it the hard way. So sure enough, I went back to Chicago and joined Bert Kelly. That was another guy on the order, Jack Lane.
